title: Kernel-aware prefill scheduler and tokenizer fastlane
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce prefill-side CPU and latency overhead by introducing a kernel-aware prefill scheduler and a minimal tokenizer fastlane that short-circuits full Unicode normalization for common payloads. The goal is to reduce prefill wall time for typical web-text prompts and reduce decoder tail-latency caused by prefill scheduling contention on GPU kernels.
background: Current prefill flow serializes tokenization, full Unicode normalization, and submit-to-GPU stages. For short prompts (<=128 tokens) we observe 35-55ms median prefill CPU time on our Hosted tier, and frequent kernel selection thrashing on mixed-length workloads. Analysis of production histograms shows >70% of prompts are ASCII-dominant and would not need full normalization. Additionally, kernel selection decisions today are stateless per-request and do not consider recent scheduling history or KV-cache hit likelihood.
goals: Introduce a kernel-aware prefill scheduler that selects microbatch size and kernel variant based on prompt length histogram and recent kernel occupancy
Implement a tokenizer fastlane that performs a lightweight ASCII/Latin pass and skips heavy normalization when safe
Prewarm KV-cache and hint decoder kernels for speculative short responses to avoid cold-start kernel selection latency
Achieve >=20% reduction in median prefill CPU time for short prompts and <=5ms added variance in decode latency from scheduling decisions
design_decisions: Scheduler maintains a sliding-window histogram per worker process (not global) to keep memory and lock contention low

Kernel selection uses a three-tier heuristic: short/fast kernel, balanced kernel, high-throughput kernel. Heuristic input: prompt length, recent kernel failure rate, estimated KV cache hit probability

Tokenizer fastlane will run an ASCII-first path that handles common punctuation and whitespace; if non-ASCII is detected, it falls back to full normalizer. This is a best-effort optimization and will not alter tokenization semantics for inputs that require normalization
Speculative prewarm: submit an idle, low-priority decode warmup job when scheduler predicts a burst of short responses, with strict budgeted CPU/GPU limits to avoid affecting throughput
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness: end-to-end prefill latency for a short-prompt synthetic mix (70% <=32 tokens, 20% 33-128, 10% >128) shows >=20% median reduction vs baseline
No change in tokenization output for an audit corpus of 50k multilingual prompts except allowed gap where ASCII-fastlane made no normalization changes
Server-side CPU usage per worker for prefill path decreases under standard traffic profile
Kernel selection oscillation (measured as kernel-switches per 1000 requests) reduces by >=40% in mixed-length replay
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype scheduler simulation using production trace replay to validate heuristics (2 days)
Fastlane tokenizer: implement ASCII-first pass as library callable from prefill hotpath and add unit tests and fuzzing corpus (4 days)
Integrate scheduler into worker process with opt-in flag and metrics hooks (3 days)
Speculative prewarm: implement gated prewarm job queue with resource accounting and safety limits (3 days)
Canary rollout: start with 1% of hosted traffic directed to feature flag, expand to 25% if metrics stable, full rollout afterward (2 weeks schedule)
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and compare cost/lantency metrics with rollback threshold criteria
testing_and_qc: Unit tests for ASCII fastlane against a 100k input corpus covering edge punctuation and emoji
Property tests to ensure round-trip tokenization invariants for normalized inputs
Replay tests using 24 hours of anonymized production traces in perf lab with kernel selection tracing enabled
Load test with mixed-length synthetic traffic to validate scheduler stability under 2x normal load
Chaos test: inject transient kernel failures to ensure scheduler falls back gracefully
rollout_notes: Start with opt-in flag per-customer region; on Dedicated clusters expose a toggle in console for manual control. For Private deployments, provide patch and admin guide. Monitor for increased P50 decode variance before broadening rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: ASCII fastlane could miss subtle normalization cases leading to tokenization drift. Mitigation: conservative fastlane that only bypasses normalization for inputs that match strict ASCII-safe regex; audit corpus run before enabling.
Risk: Speculative prewarms could consume GPU slots and harm throughput. Mitigation: strict per-worker budget and preemptible low-priority jobs with immediate cancellation on demand.
Risk: Scheduler heuristic overfitting to the current trace. Mitigation: maintain tunable weights and remote-config flags to adjust heuristic in production without deploys

owner_notes: Goal is pragmatic latency wins with minimal semantic risk. Keep fastlane narrowly scoped: only inputs that pass ASCII-safe check and tokenization idempotency tests should use it. If incidents occur, feature flag can be turned off immediately per worker.
